The Orange Kitten I Can't Stop Making — Free Amigurumi Pattern

He's orange, he's got that little white chin like he dipped it in milk, and those big sleepy eyes that made my husband say "oh, you made another one?" Yes. I did.

This is the third version of him. The first was too skinny, the second had ears like a bat. This one finally sits properly and doesn't flop over when I put him on the shelf. I wrote down everything exactly how I do it now, so you can make yours in an evening with a cup of tea.

Skill level Beginner — you know a magic ring and single crochet
Hook + Yarn 4.0mm hook, chunky cotton — orange 80g, white 20g, pink scrap
Finished size About 5 inches sitting, 3 inches wide at the cheeks

The story behind this kitten

I've been on a bit of an orange kick lately — pumpkins on the porch, leftover orange yarn from the fox I made last month. I had a ball of this terracotta orange and I just started a head without a plan. My daughter came in, saw it, and said "is that a cat?" and that was it. It had to be a cat.

What took me the longest was the face. I wanted that wide-eyed kitten look, not too realistic, not too cartoon. The trick ended up being two things: big 16mm eyes placed low, and a separate white muzzle that puffs out a bit. When I tried to crochet the white part directly into the head with color changes, it pulled and looked messy. Sewing it on as an oval was ten times easier and cuter.

I keep this one by my sewing machine now. He holds my pins when I'm not looking.

What you need from your stash

  • Yarn: Chunky / worsted cotton — Orange main (I used ~80g), White (~20g for muzzle, chest, paws), Pink scrap for nose
  • Hook: 4.0mm. If your stitches show stuffing, go down to 3.5mm.
  • Eyes: 16mm black safety eyes with washers — we place them between Rounds 11 and 12, 8 stitches apart. If it's for a little one, embroider them instead.
  • Extras: Polyfill, tapestry needle, 5 stitch markers, pins, scissors, a pinch of white embroidery thread for whiskers
I crochet quite tight. If you are a looser crocheter, your kitten will be a touch bigger — totally fine. Just keep your tension even throughout the head so one side doesn't bulge.

Starting the head — my magic ring pulled tight, first two rounds done. It should cup like a little bowl.

How I size him

With my 4.0mm and chunky cotton: 5" tall sitting. With DK and 3.5mm: about 4". With velvet and 5.0mm: about 6.5" and extra squishy. I haven't graded him, this is just what happened when I swapped yarns.

My abbreviations

mr — magic ring, ch — chain, sc — single crochet, inc — 2 sc in same stitch, dec — invisible decrease (grab front loops only), sl st — slip stitch, FO — fasten off, [...] x6 — repeat. I work in a spiral, so move your marker up each round. No joining unless I say so.

Step 1: The head — where he gets his personality

STEP 1 · HEAD

We increase quickly to 36, then we just go round and round. That's where you get to breathe. The eyes go in while you still have a hole to reach inside.

Head — in orange:
R1: mr, 6 sc (6)
R2: inc in each st around (12)
R3: [sc 1, inc] x6 (18)
R4: [sc 2, inc] x6 (24)
R5: [sc 3, inc] x6 (30)
R6: [sc 4, inc] x6 (36) — circle should be about 2 1/4" across
R7-R12: sc around 36 — 6 rounds even
Place eyes now: between R11 and R12, 8 stitches apart. Put them on pins first, look straight at him. I count 8 between, and I like them centered low so he has a forehead.
R13-R14: sc around 36 — 2 rounds even after eyes
R15: [sc 4, dec] x6 (30)
R16: [sc 3, dec] x6 (24) — start stuffing. Firm in cheeks, medium on top.
R17: [sc 2, dec] x6 (18)
R18: [sc 1, dec] x6 (12)
R19: dec x6 (6) — close, leave a 12" tail for sewing later

After R12 he should look like a chubby dome, not a cone. If he looks pointy, you probably skipped an increase back in R4 or R5 — easy to do. Just rip back to where the circle stopped being flat and count again. I've done it twice.

After the even rounds — this is when I pop the safety eyes in and give him a little stuffing to see if I like the face.

Step 2: Ears that actually look like ears + that white muzzle

STEP 2 · EARS & FACE

My first ears were too big and flopped. These are smaller and they stand up because we don't stuff them.

Ears — make 2 in orange:
R1: mr, 4 sc (4)
R2: [sc 1, inc] x2 (6)
R3: [sc 2, inc] x2 (8)
R4: [sc 3, inc] x2 (10)
FO, leave 10" tail, press flat. No stuffing.

White muzzle:
Ch 6. Starting in 2nd ch from hook: sc 4, 3 sc in last ch, turn to other side of chain, sc 3, inc in last ch (12)
R2: inc, sc 3, inc x3, sc 3, inc x2 (18)
R3: sc around 18 — FO, leave tail. Should be a soft oval about 1.5" wide.

Pink nose: With pink, I embroider a little triangle on the muzzle — 3 stitches wide at top, point down — then one short vertical line for the mouth.

Pin the ears between Rounds 3 and 7 of the head, inner edges about 7 stitches apart. Angle them just slightly forward like he's listening. Pin the muzzle so its top edge is one round below the bottom of the eyes, centered. I always step back from my table to check — if the muzzle is crooked you'll see it in every photo.

Step 3: Body and the white belly patch I love

STEP 3 · BODY
Body — in orange:
R1: mr, 6 sc (6)
R2: inc x6 (12)
R3: [sc 1, inc] x6 (18)
R4: [sc 2, inc] x6 (24)
R5-R9: sc around 24 — 5 rounds straight (24)
R10: [sc 2, dec] x6 (18)
R11-R13: sc around 18 — 3 rounds (18)
FO, leave long tail, stuff firmly. It should be a little chubby tube that can sit flat.

White chest — in white:
R1: mr, 6 sc (6)
R2: inc x6 (12)
R3: [sc 1, inc] x6 (18)
R4: [sc 2, inc] x6 (24)
FO, leave tail. Pin it to center front of body, top at about R5.

Body done with the white chest pinned on — I sew it on with white yarn so the stitches disappear.

If the chest pulls the body when you pin it, either your body is understuffed or the chest is a bit big — just go down to R3 for a smaller oval. I did that on my second kitten.

Step 4: Arms and legs with little white socks

STEP 4 · LIMBS
Arms — make 2: Start with white, then switch to orange.
R1: mr, 6 sc (6) — white
R2: [sc 1, inc] x3 (9) — white
R3-R8: sc around 9 — orange, 6 rounds. Stuff only the hand lightly, leave arm soft so it drapes.
FO, leave tail.

Legs — make 2: Start with white.
R1: mr, 6 sc (6) — white
R2: inc x6 (12) — white
R3: sc around 12 — white
R4-R10: sc around 12 — orange, 7 rounds. Stuff medium, flatten bottom.
FO, leave tail.

The white tips are my favorite part — just two rounds of white makes it look like little socks. If you want toe beans, add three tiny bobbles on the bottom of the foot, but honestly I skip it most days.

Step 5: Putting him together so he sits

STEP 5 · ASSEMBLY

I lay everything out first. No sewing until I'm happy with how he's sitting. This is the part where pins are your best friend.

  • Head to body: I sew head to body with the tail from the head, going around twice. I pull snug so there is no wobble.
  • Ears: already on head, but give them a final stitch through both layers so they stay upright.
  • Arms: at the sides, at about Rounds 3-4 of the body, pointing slightly forward. If you sew them straight out he looks like he's doing jumping jacks.
  • Legs: at the bottom front, bottoms flat. Test sitting after pinning — if he tips forward, move legs one round back.

My table before assembly — head with ears, body with chest, arms, legs, eyes, little pink nose piece. I pin everything before I pick up the needle.

Step 6: Final touches — whiskers and that little face

STEP 6 · FINISHING

Now the fun little details. Whiskers: I cut 6 pieces of white embroidery floss about 2 inches long, three per side. I thread them through the muzzle with a needle and knot inside so they don't pull out.

Eyebrows: two tiny black stitches, one stitch above each eye, just two stitches long and angled down a little. It gives him that slightly worried, very cute expression like in the photo you sent me.

I sometimes take a clean toothbrush and lightly brush the orange yarn outward — makes him fluffier. And if you have soft pastel, a tiny dot of pink on the cheeks is adorable, but blend it well.

And there he is — 5 inches of orange mischief. Mine lives by my yarn basket and steals my stitch markers.

My finishing tricks

I weave tails inside the body with my tapestry needle and pop knots into the stuffing so they don't show. I always use invisible decreases — just front loops — so you don't get little holes. And I stuff the head firmer than the body, so the cheeks stay round.

If something looks off

Head looks pointy: Missed increase in R3-R6. Count that round again, add one if you have 35 instead of 36 — it won't show.

Eyes too wide or too high: Pin first, look straight on. 8 stitches between, between R11-R12. If you already snapped washers and regret it, add a tiny white highlight dot with white yarn on the outer edge of each eye — it visually pulls them together.

Won't sit: Flatten the bottom of body and legs with your palm and move legs back one round. Works every time.

Seams show: Sew white to white with white yarn, orange to orange with orange. And sew inside the edge of the white pieces, not outside.

Make him yours

I've made him in gray with a little yellow fish, in cream with orange spots embroidered after, and once in velvet that was so soft I didn't want to give him away. Add a tiny scarf — chain 20, sc back, done. Or a bell on a little collar.

If you make him, tag me or send me a photo — I keep a little folder of all your kittens on my desktop and it makes my day.

— Sara
